newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia steps up efforts to join NATO.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia steps up efforts to join NATO.

text.p: Slovenia has intensified its diplomatic efforts to become a full member of NATO, Slovenian Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun said on Wednesday.
"Last week was the most active in the history of Slovenian diplomacy," Kracun told a news conference.
He said Slovenian diplomats had met senior officials from 27 countries during last week's session of the United Nations General Assembly.
Most nations expressed supported for Slovenia's bid for NATO membership and none were opposed, Kracun said.
"The talks proved that Slovenia's membership of NATO would not irritate anyone," he added.

The 16-member North Atlantic Treaty Organisation is expected to decide when and how to enlarge the alliance by the end of this year and to start negotiations with the most promising candidates in 1997.
The U.S. senate recently listed Slovenia among the first four NATO candidates, along with Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.

Slovenia, which declared independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991 and faces its third multi-party general election on November 10, hopes to join NATO as soon as possible in order to ensure greater political stability in the restless Balkan region.
